jobs.description: Talent Acquisition Partner Help take Solve Intelligence 3x in a single year. We’re looking for a recruiter with strong engineering hiring experience who wants to recruit across the business and help build our talent function. 🏗️ About the role You’ll be an early hire in our talent team, owning searches from first outreach through to signed offer. Engineering recruitment will be a core part of your remit, alongside GTM, legal, operations and other functions as the business grows. You’ll need to enjoy that breadth and get to grips with unfamiliar roles quickly. You’ll be responsible for: Running multiple searches across engineering, AI research, GTM, legal and operations, from understanding the requirements to closing the offer. Building pipelines through direct sourcing, using targeted outreach and newer AI sourcing tools to find candidates beyond inbound applications and agencies. Deciding which searches need your attention most, understanding the business priorities behind them, and flagging risks early. Working with hiring managers to define what each role requires and design assessments that help us make hiring decisions. You’ll need enough technical understanding to assess engineering candidates and discuss your judgement with the team. Improving hiring quality and offer acceptance by understanding candidates’ motivations early and closing people with competing offers. Keeping candidates informed throughout the process, with thoughtful outreach, timely updates and honest communication. Helping build the talent function: keeping Ashby accurate, improving workflows and contributing to projects beyond your own searches. 🚀 Who you are You’ve hired frontend, backend, full-stack and AI engineers, and you understand the differences between those searches. You can read a technical CV critically and hold a substantive first conversation with an engineer. Your recent experience is either in-house at an early-stage startup or at a recruitment firm working with technical companies that set a high hiring bar. You’re comfortable working with limited support and deciding what needs your attention without waiting for direction. You care about how recruitment is run. That shows in the outreach you send and the assessment notes hiring managers use to make decisions. You keep Ashby up to date, and candidates know where they stand. 🛠️ What you bring Must haves Direct experience hiring frontend, backend, full-stack and AI engineers. Experience using Ashby, ideally including improving how it is configured or used. Hands-on sourcing experience and the ability to build a pipeline from scratch. Fluency with newer AI sourcing tools, beyond LinkedIn Recruiter. Strong written communication. Your outreach and candidate updates should be good enough to share as examples. Demonstrated ability to close candidates with competing offers. The ability to pick up new roles, understand requirements quickly and build processes from scratch. Nice to haves An agency or search firm background earlier in your career. Experience building AI-powered recruiting workflows. Solve's AI platform manages everything from invention harvesting and patent generation through to litigation and licensing. jobs.description: 🌟  VO2 GROUP : Leader français indépendant en conseil Tech et Digital Entre conseil stratégique et réalisation technologique, nous cultivons un esprit "boutique" : de l'excellence, de l'humain et une forte culture de l'innovation. Nous sommes présents à Paris, Montréal, Shanghai, New York et Genève, avec plus de 800 consultants. 🌍 Leader mondial de l'expérience client et corporate Nous collaborons avec les marques les plus emblématiques pour assurer leur succès : ✔️ De la stratégie et l'innovation ✔️ À l'exécution à grande échelle, grâce à notre expertise en business, tech, data et IA 🤖✨ 🏆 Reconnaissances & Leadership Leader en innovation et croissance 2025 (Les Echos Business Magazine) Acteur multi-tech et partenaire Premium Salesforce 🌿 Champion d'une "Tech Responsable et Durable" Créé avec la parité hommes-femmes, défendant l’égalité grâce à une équipe de direction engagée 🌟 45 % de femmes au sein de nos équipes Campagne primée TopCom en 2024 📜 Certifications et Prix Salesforce Impact Partner 2024 Cybervadis 2025 Entreprise à impact de l'année 2024 par Choose My Company 🚀VO2 GROUP: The Bright Side of Tech 🌈 _________________________________________________________________   Pour l’un de nos clients majeurs du secteur Retail, nous recherchons un(e) Product Owner IT Salesforce Marketing Cloud (SFMC) à dominante technico-fonctionnelle. La mission s’inscrit dans un programme de digitalisation du parcours After Sales, avec pour objectif d’optimiser les communications adressées aux clients tout au long du parcours de prise en charge d’un produit en service après-vente. La solution s’appuie sur Salesforce Marketing Cloud pour orchestrer les différentes notifications clients, notamment sur les canaux Email et SMS, dans un contexte international et multi-marchés. Le/la PO IT travaillera en étroite collaboration avec la PO métier et assurera l’interface avec les équipes techniques SFMC.   Vos Missions Vous interviendrez notamment sur : Le cadrage, l’analyse et le challenge des besoins métier, ainsi que leur traduction en User Stories, spécifications fonctionnelles et critères d’acceptation ; Le pilotage et le suivi des évolutions dans Salesforce Marketing Cloud, en lien avec les équipes techniques ; La conception et l’évolution des parcours de notifications Email & SMS : règles de déclenchement, contenus, langues, marchés et délais d’envoi ; L’accompagnement des roll-outs internationaux et la préparation des configurations nécessaires aux nouveaux marchés ; La recette fonctionnelle, les tests end-to-end et l’accompagnement des phases d’UAT ; La coordination des équipes métier, techniques et régionales, ainsi que le suivi des dépendances et points bloquants ; Le maintien de la documentation fonctionnelle et des spécificités liées aux différents marchés.     Profil recherché Nous recherchons un profil technico-fonctionnel, capable de comprendre et challenger un besoin métier tout en disposant d’une bonne maîtrise de Salesforce Marketing Cloud. Compétences clés :  Expérience en tant que PPO, PO IT, Business Analyst ou Consultant technico-fonctionnel ; Expérience significative sur Salesforce Marketing Cloud (SFMC) ; Bonne compréhension des parcours clients et des notifications automatisées Email & SMS ; Maîtrise de la rédaction de User Stories et spécifications fonctionnelles ; Capacité à comprendre et challenger la faisabilité d’une demande dans SFMC ; Expérience en recette fonctionnelle, tests end-to-end et UAT ; Maîtrise de Jira ou d’un outil équivalent ; Une expérience sur des projets de roll-out internationaux est un vrai plus.  Une maitrise de l'anglais professionnel courant, à l’écrit comme à l’oral, est indispensable pour cette mission, les échanges s’effectuant régulièrement dans un contexte international. jobs.title: Stage de Vente - Nice Cap 3000
jobs.description: À PROPOS DE LA MARQUE Chez Karl Lagerfeld, nous suivons le mantra suivant : « Profiter du présent et inventer le futur ».   Toujours contemporaine et tournée vers l’avenir, la maison KARL LAGERFELD partage la vision créative et l’esthétique de son fondateur emblématique, Karl Lagerfeld.   Nous sommes la seule maison de couture portant le nom de Karl et nous nous efforçons d’être à la hauteur de cette responsabilité dans tout ce que nous réalisons, chaque jour, avec la plus grande joie et passion.   Nos sièges de Paris et d’Amsterdam accueillent une équipe diversifiée et motivée de membres de la famille KARL venant de plus de 35 pays différents. Ensemble, nous visons à créer des histoires pleines de sens ainsi que des concepts de produit liés au monde et aux attributs emblématiques de Karl.   Le prêt à porter pour femme, les sacs, la petite maroquinerie et les sous-vêtements sont gérés directement depuis notre siège d’Amsterdam, tandis que d’autres catégories, incluant le prêt à porter pour homme, les parfums, la lunetterie et autres, sont développés avec les meilleurs partenaires de licence de leur catégorie. La récente ligne KARL LAGERFELD JEANS est de la même manière gérée en dehors de notre siège d’Amsterdam et est notre gamme connaissant la croissance la plus rapide.   Nous sommes en contact avec nos consommateurs à différents niveaux, nous assurant que notre approche à la fois en ligne et hors ligne aillent de pair. Nous nous efforçons d’optimiser l’engagement de nos clients avec plus de 200 magasins KL dans le monde, nos partenaires grossistes premium, et notre couverture numérique, avec à sa position le flagship store KARL.COM, qui est disponible dans 96 pays. Nos canaux numériques représentent plus de 30% de notre activité à plein tarif.   Nous sommes une entreprise dynamique, à la croissance rapide et inclusive construite sur le professionnalisme et des valeurs fortes. Chez KARL KAGERFELD, nous nous engageons à travailler avec les plus hautes normes en matière de durabilité et d’intégrité dans tous nos domaines d’activité. En 2019, KARL LAGERFELD a rejoint la Fashion Pact, une initiative de durabilité mondiale cherchant à transformer le secteur de la mode par le biais d’objectifs dans trois différents domaines : climat, biodiversité et protection des océans, en tant que membre fondateur. POSITION La Maison KARL LAGERFELD souhaite contribuer à la formation et au succès de futurs jeunes talents de la mode. C’est dans ce but que nous proposons des stages conventionnés à temps plein pour une période de 6 mois en tant qu’assistant(e)s de ventes. Le stage se déroulera au sein de nos corners en Grands Magasins à Nice Massena ou Nice Cap 3000.   Ambassadeur de la Maison KARL LAGERFELD, vous aurez pour mission: - Assurer le meilleur accueil et service auprès d’une clientèle française et internationale - Participer à la réalisation du chiffre d’affaires - Participer à la mise en place du Merchandising - Assurer le Réassort - S’assurer de la bonne gestion des stocks - Nous vous garantissons un suivi pédagogique allié un à environnement formateur et enrichissant.   PROFIL Pour mener à bien ce stage, le profil suivant est requis : Vous êtes doté d’une réelle finesse relationnelle, vous êtes reconnu pour votre sens du service Dynamique et enthousiaste, vous avez le goût du challenge et de la vente. Vous avez un bon niveau d’anglais Vous êtes curieux, doté d'une personnalité cool et dynamique Enfin, votre esprit d’équipe, votre implication et votre état d’esprit positif vous assureront une parfaite intégration au sein de notre Maison   Convention de stage obligatoire - Compensation ou rémunération selon la législation. Join a forward-thinking technology team building the AI platform that powers intelligent agents across multiple business functions, including engineering, business development, compliance, support, and finance. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you will design, develop, and operate the infrastructure that enables AI agents to perform increasingly autonomous tasks safely and reliably. You will work across agent runtimes, integrations, identity management, security guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and observability. Collaborating closely with internal domain experts, you will turn operational challenges into scalable AI-powered solutions that deliver measurable business value. You will take ownership from initial design and implementation through production deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement. This remote-first opportunity is ideal for an experienced engineer who combines strong software fundamentals with practical expertise in deploying and scaling LLM-based systems. jobs.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Marketing Specialist based in France. As an AI Marketing Specialist, you will combine digital marketing expertise with artificial intelligence and automation to drive measurable business growth. You will develop and execute AI-powered marketing strategies across multiple channels, helping improve customer acquisition, lead generation, and campaign performance. Using generative AI tools and marketing automation platforms, you will create personalized content, optimize advertising campaigns, and streamline marketing operations. You will also leverage AI-driven insights to identify new market opportunities, understand customer behavior, and improve audience targeting. Working across paid advertising, SEO, content creation, and customer engagement, you will continuously experiment with emerging technologies. This is an opportunity to contribute to innovative marketing initiatives while delivering measurable results in a fully remote environment. Accountabilities You will lead the implementation and optimization of AI-driven marketing initiatives, using automation, data analysis, and emerging technologies to improve campaign effectiveness and business performance. Develop and execute AI-driven digital marketing strategies across multiple channels to increase brand visibility, generate qualified leads, and improve customer acquisition. Leverage generative AI tools to create, personalize, and optimize marketing materials, including advertising copy, landing pages, email campaigns, and social media content. Plan, launch, manage, and optimize paid advertising campaigns using AI-powered features and tools across Google Ads and Meta Ads. Use AI solutions for audience research, customer segmentation, competitor analysis, and identifying new market opportunities. Implement AI-powered SEO strategies, including keyword research, search intent analysis, content optimization, and editorial planning. Build and optimize automated marketing workflows for lead generation, lead nurturing, and customer engagement. Analyze campaign performance using AI-powered tools to identify trends, evaluate results, and generate actionable recommendations. Implement AI-driven personalization strategies to enhance customer journeys, improve engagement, and increase conversion rates. Experiment with AI-powered creative generation tools to develop and optimize advertising visuals and campaign assets. Monitor key marketing performance indicators, including Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC), Return on Ad Spend (ROAS), Click-Through Rate (CTR), Cost Per Click (CPC), conversion rates, and lead generation metrics. Continuously research and test emerging AI marketing technologies to identify opportunities for greater efficiency, automation, and campaign performance. jobs.title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
jobs.description: The question Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards. What you will do The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request. 1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report. 2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured. 3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along. 4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFE

What You'll Do Own the architecture of our Microsoft Fabric estate end to end — OneLake, our lakehouses and their bronze, silver, and gold layers, workspace and domain structure, naming conventions, and the standards that keep it coherent as it grows. Work closely with our Business Operations & Data Specialists, who represent the business owners of each domain: turn their requirements into the right gold tables, agree definitions with them, and give them a platform they can query, validate, and explain to the business with confidence. Keep the platform reliable, observable, and cost-aware: monitoring, alerting, recovery, and disciplined use of our Fabric capacity — including knowing what a runaway notebook costs us. Requirements What You’ll Need Requirements Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field. 5-8 years of data engineering experience, including real ownership of a lakehouse architecture rather than only delivering against someone else's. Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is strongly preferred — OneLake, lakehouses, Delta tables, the SQL analytics endpoint, Data Factory pipelines, Spark notebooks, and semantic models in Direct Lake mode. Strong command of the medallion pattern and of Delta Lake in practice: partitioning, schema evolution, table maintenance, and why a gold table behaves the way it does. Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQ

At Destinus, we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing — bringing speed, precision, and innovation to every process that powers our advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). We are a fast-growing international group operating across several European entities, and the standards we hold our financial data to are rising just as quickly. Join us in building a finance reporting foundation that is accurate, traceable, and ready for any question asked of it. What You'll Do Be the go-to contact between the business owners of finance data — the CFO, accounts payable and receivable, and treasury — and our lakehouse: turn their questions into clear data requirements, and the data back into answers they can act on. Build and maintain Power BI dashboards covering cash flow, receipts and collections, payables, and spend across the group, built on certified lakehouse data. Partner with our Data Engineers on the curated (gold) layer for finance: specify the tables, fields, and business rules — entities, currencies, financial dimensions, intercompany — and validate the result against the ledger before anyone relies on it. Prepare and quality-check entity-level data extractions from our lakehouse and ERP in support of the external audit, and keep audit requests tracked from request to delivery. Define and document finance KPI definitions in our KPI catalog — formulas, inclusions, exclusions, owners, and sources — to a standard that withstands external review. Describe our finance data in plain business language — what each field means, who owns it, and how sensitive it is — for our shared meanings layer, so that colleagues and our AI assistants can use it correctly without having to ask you first. Automate what is manual today: turn recurring spreadsheet work, audit packs, and month-end routines into repeatable processes that largely run themselves. Improve the finance processes and system configuration that create the data, working with the finance team and our ERP specialists, so that issues are fixed at source rather than corrected every month. Help the finance team get more from the tools through training and self-service, so they can answer their own questions. Requirements What You’ll Need Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Controlling, Economics, or a related field. A genuine finance background is essential — experience in external or internal audit, controlling, financial reporting, or FP&A. This is not a data role with finance on the side; you need to understand the accounting behind the figures. Confident with general ledger and subledger structures, trial balances, accounts payable and accounts receivable, bank reconciliations, intercompany transactions, and the principles of IFRS. Strong expertise in Power BI (data modeling, DAX, dashboard design, troubleshooting), complemented by advanced Excel skills. Comfortable querying data with SQL and working in a lakehouse or data warehouse environment; experience

jobs.title: Data Platform Manager

You will own its architecture: how OneLake and our lakehouses are structured, how data lands in them from the systems we run, and how it holds up as more of the business comes to depend on it. You will lead a small team of data engineers — setting direction, reviewing their work, growing them — and you will keep building yourself. You are also the person who makes our AI ambitions possible: the foundation behind our data agents and our Company Brain is yours to design and deliver. At Destinus we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing, building advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) across three European plants. The data you will work with is physical — parts, build progress, shortages, non-conformances — and the questions asked of it get harder each year as we grow. If you want a platform you can still shape rather than one already set in concrete, this is a good moment to arrive. What You'll Do Own the architecture of our Microsoft Fabric estate end to end — OneLake, our lakehouses and their bronze, silver, and gold layers, workspace and domain structure, naming conventions, and the standards that keep it coherent as it grows. Lead, mentor, and grow a small team of data engineers: set priorities, review code, raise the technical bar, and develop the people. Stay hands-on. You will build pipelines, notebooks, and Delta tables yourself, not only direct others who do. Own the integrations that land data in OneLake from our source systems — ERP, HR, shopfloor, quality, and the business applications that come after them — choosing sensibly between Data Factory pipelines, dataflows, shortcuts, and mirroring for each source. Own the gold layer and the semantic models built on it, so that Power BI reads from one governed source rather than from copies scattered around the business. Work closely with our Business Operations & Data Specialists, who represent the business owners of each domain: turn their requirements into the right gold tables, agree definitions with them, and give them a platform they can query, validate, and explain to the business with confidence. Own lineage across the estate: know what feeds what, be able to prove it to an auditor, and make dependencies visible rather than tribal knowledge. Build the data foundation for our AI programme — the lakehouse structures, pipelines, and knowledge graph behind our Fabric data agents and our Company Brain — and deliver it to a standard that can be trusted with a real question. Design and maintain the OneLake security and access model together with your team: workspace roles, access groups, and the controls that decide who sees what in the lake. Keep the platform reliable, observable, and cost-aware: monitoring, alerting, recovery, and disciplined use of our Fabric capacity — including knowing what a runaway notebook costs us. Requirements What You’ll Need Requirements Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field. 5-8 years of data engineering experience, including real ownership of a lakehouse architecture rather than only delivering against someone else's. Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is strongly preferred — OneLake, lakehouses, Delta tables, the SQL analytics endpoint, Data Factory pipelines, Spark notebooks, and semantic models in Direct Lake mode. If your depth is in Azure Synapse, Databricks, or Data Lake Storage Gen2 and you have since moved onto Fabric in earnest, we will take that seriously. Strong command of the medallion pattern and of Delta Lake in practice: partitioning, schema evolution, table maintenance, and why a gold table behaves the way it does. Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQ

You will define how we model our systems and build the libraries, analyses and integrations that make the model useful day to day. Working closely with processor, hardware and software teams, you will play an important role in enabling the design of the large-scale quantum computers built around VIO-powered QPUs. What are you going to do? Define and own QuantWare’s MBSE methodology, modelling conventions and architecture framework for quantum computing systems, covering the quantum processor, cryostat, signal chain, control and readout electronics, and software stack. Build reusable model libraries for key subsystems, including QPU interfaces, cryogenic wiring and attenuation, microwave signal paths, and control electronics. Develop automated analyses on top of the model, such as heat-load, signal-integrity and noise budgets, channel counts, scalability, and full-system metrics such as power consumption as qubit counts grow. Establish requirements traceability from customer and system-level requirements down to component specifications and verification tests. Connect the system model to simulation and measurement data, creating a digital thread between design and test. A solid track record in requirements engineering and verification of complex, multidisciplinary hardware systems. Strong organisational and communication skills. You thrive in a cross-disciplinary environment and are comfortable taking ownership from day one. Bonus Points Experience with cryogenic, RF/microwave or precision instrumentation systems, or direct experience with superconducting quantum hardware. Background in high-tech, semiconductor, aerospace or scientific instrumentation industries. Experience introducing MBSE into an organisation and driving its adoption. Experience translating complex payment rules, fee schedules or network requirements into system logic, configurations and controls. Strong analytical and quantitative capabilities, including experience working with transaction-level data, economic modelling and reconciliation of expected versus actual payment costs. Commercial judgment and the ability to connect payment mechanics to pricing, product decisions and margin optimisation. Exceptional attention to detail and ownership, with the discipline required to manage complex rules where small errors can create meaningful financial impact at scale. Strong cross-functional execution, with the ability to work effectively across Product, Engineering, Finance, Data, Operations and external payment partners. jobs.description: Ben jij op zoek naar een uitdagende IT-stage waarin je jouw technische kennis in de praktijk kunt brengen én jezelf verder kunt ontwikkelen? Bij Cefetra in Rotterdam hebben we vanaf februari 2027 een stageplek beschikbaar voor een enthousiaste en leergierige IT-student. wie zijn wij? Cefetra Group bestaat uit verschillende handelsbedrijven die actief zijn binnen de agrarische sector en de voedingsingrediëntenindustrie, waaronder toonaangevende merken binnen de ingrediëntenmarkt. Samen hebben we ongeveer 800 medewerkers, verspreid over 39 kantoren in 17 landen wereldwijd. We werken nauw met elkaar samen om onze klanten de best mogelijke service te bieden. Samen met onze leveranciers bouwen we sterke supply chains en creëren we waarde door grondstoffen in te kopen en te leveren aan de internationale voedingsmiddelen-, diervoedings- en energiesector. Bekijk hier onze corporate video . De stage Als IT Support Stagiair(e) word je onderdeel van het IT-team en ondersteun je collega’s bij hun dagelijkse IT-vragen. Je bent het eerste aanspreekpunt voor gebruikers en helpt bij het oplossen van technische problemen, zowel op afstand als op kantoor. Hierdoor krijg je een goed beeld van hoe IT-support binnen een internationale organisatie werkt. Tijdens je stage houd je je onder andere bezig met: Het bieden van eerstelijns IT-support en oplossen van hardware-, software- en netwerkproblemen; Het beheren van gebruikersaccounts, wachtwoorden, licenties en apparaten; Het installeren, configureren en uitgeven van laptops en mobiele telefoons; Het registreren en opvolgen van incidenten en aanvragen via het ticketsysteem. Daarnaast werk je samen met ervaren IT-specialisten aan projecten op het gebied van infrastructuur, werkplekbeheer en procesverbetering. Hierdoor ontwikkel je niet alleen je technische vaardigheden, maar leer je ook hoe IT een belangrijke bijdrage levert aan de dagelijkse werkzaamheden binnen een internationale handelsorganisatie. Tijdens je stage maak je ook kennis met de technologieën en systemen die binnen onze IT-omgeving worden gebruikt. Je werkt met Microsoft 365, Azure, Active Directory, Intune en Windows Server voor het beheren van gebruikers, apparaten en applicaties. Daarnaast doe je ervaring op met Cisco Meraki voor netwerkbeheer, Citrix voor virtuele werkplekken en applicaties, VMware voor gevirtualiseerde serveromgevingen en TeamViewer voor ondersteuning op afstand. Zo krijg je een brede kijk op zowel moderne cloudoplossingen als traditionele IT-infrastructuur. Wie ben jij? Je bent nieuwsgierig, servicegericht en krijgt energie van het oplossen van technische uitdagingen. Je neemt initiatief, werkt graag samen met anderen en bent niet bang om verantwoordelijkheid te nemen. Daarnaast beschik je over analytisch en probleemoplossend vermogen, goede communicatieve vaardigheden en ben je flexibel en betrouwbaar. Idealiter herken je jezelf in het volgende: Je volgt momenteel een mbo-opleiding richting ICT, Informatica, Systeem- en Netwerkbeheer of een vergelijkbare opleiding; Je hebt affiniteit met IT-support en systeembeheer; Je bent leergierig en wilt graag praktijkervaring opdoen binnen een professionele IT-omgeving; Je beschikt over basiskennis van Windows, Microsoft 365 en netwerken; Je kunt zowel zelfstandig als in teamverband werken; Je beheerst zowel de Nederlandse als de Engelse taal goed. Wat bieden wij? Een unieke kans om ervaring op te doen binnen een snelgroeiende, internationale organisatie. Zelfstandigheid en verantwoordelijkheid staan centraal binnen onze bedrijfscultuur. Personally deliver the first system end to end: the analysis and back-test, the features, the model, policy or agent, the deployment, and the shadow and A/B tests that prove it works. Not a spec handed to someone else to build. Operate what you deploy. Own monitoring, retraining, drift response, incident handling and rollback for live decisioning, alongside the engineering teams whose services call it — and set the expectation that the function runs its systems rather than shipping them. Work across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and be honest about which a problem actually needs: a propensity or uplift model, a policy of rules, or an agent with tools, evals against golden answer sets and trace-level observability. Several of our strongest candidate use cases point each way. Build and lead the team — hire senior data scientists embedded in value areas and machine learning engineers in the hub, and set the professional standards, shared methods and reusable components the function runs on. jobs.title: FinOps Data Engineer
jobs.description: About the Role We're looking for a FinOps Data Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams. This role owns the data side of that mission: the models, pipelines, and analysis that make cost, usage, and margin numbers trustworthy across the company. This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the dbt model or Python pipeline that ships the fix, building the cost-vs-revenue mart that answers a margin question once instead of every time, and chasing a number until it reconciles. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case or a data model's implications to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week. What You'll Be Responsible For In this role, you'll: Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. Take ideas from identification through to a realized dollar figure, not just a recommendation. Build and maintain the FinOps data pipeline: Design and run the BigQuery/dbt models that turn raw billing and usage data (CUR, Storage Lens) into reconciled, trustworthy mart tables, the foundation everything else in FinOps is built on. Build cost-vs-revenue and customer segmentation models: Model unit economics and margin by product line and customer segment, and extend coverage as new products and segments come online. Apply data science to cost and usage data: Build forecasting models, detect anomalies statistically rather than by threshold alone, and quantify savings opportunities (e.g. storage lifecycle, request-cost patterns) with rigor a spreadsheet can't match. Build and maintain cost attribution: Tagging policies, cost allocation, and chargeback/showback so engineering teams can see and own their own spend. This is foundational work other savings work depends on. Automate cost governance: Build automated cost reporting, anomaly detection, and alerting. Write the scripts and infrastructure-as-code (Python, Terraform, Lambda) that enforce cost policy rather than relying on manual review. Partner with engineering on architecture decisions: Bring cost into the room early, cost-efficiencies are cheaper to get right at design than to retrofit. Work with Finance on forecasting and reporting: Support budget tracking and financial KPIs; build dashboards and self-serve analytics engineering and finance can both read. You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have strong AWS expertise and working GCP knowledge, including pricing models, billing structures, and cost optimization mechanics. Have data engineering depth: dbt, BigQuery (or an equivalent modern warehouse), SQL at scale, and data modeling for analytics (dimensional modeling, incremental models, testing). Have data science fundamentals: statistical forecasting, anomaly detection, and experimentation, and know when a rigorous model beats a rule of thumb. Have automation and scripting skills: Python, Terraform/ pulumi, Lambda, or Bash. jobs.description: Bloomreach is building the world’s premier agentic platform for personalization .We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the entire customer journey. We’re making conversational shopping a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey. We're designing the future of autonomous marketing , taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do. And we're building all of that on the intelligence of a single AI engine — Loomi — so that personalization isn't only autonomous…it's also consistent.From retail to financial services, hospitality to gaming, businesses use Bloomreach to drive higher growth and lasting loyalty. We power personalization for more than 1,400 global brands, including American Eagle, Sonepar, and Pandora. You'd be joining the Artificial Intelligence team . We own the algorithmic core of the platform: Predictions, Contextual Personalization, contextual bandits, autosegmentation, and the agentic workflows behind Loomi. We work with behavioural data at terabyte scale, across 1,400+ customers, in production, every day. We are currently allowing flexibility for our employees to work from anywhere for the respective region (Central & Eastern Europe) or we are happy to meet you in our offices in Bratislava (Slovakia) or Brno, Prague (Czechia) on a full-time basis. The mission You find the signal in how 1,400 brands' customers actually behave — and you prove it moved a business metric. Your models decide which customers are predicted to churn, which segments form themselves, which offer a shopper sees, and whether the discount changed anything or was going to convert anyway. What you'll actually do Frame the problem before modelling it. Most of our highest-impact work arrives as a vague business question, and turning it into something measurable is the first job. Build and evaluate models across Predictions and Contextual Personalization: propensity and churn, contextual bandits, autosegmentation, uplift and incrementality. Design the evaluation, not just the model. Offline metrics, backtests, and the A/B design that decides whether this ships. You own the question "how would we know if this is worse?" Bring methods in from outside and judge them honestly — read the literature, run the quick PoC, and tell a real result from a well-marketed one. Hand off cleanly to ML Engineering. You own the model and the evidence; they own making it survive production. That handoff is a document and a conversation, not a notebook over a wall. Explain your results to people who aren't data scientists — Product, Engineering leadership, and sometimes customers. What success looks like after 12 months Two models you built are in production and you can name the business metric each one moved. jobs.description: What do we do? Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better. We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally. The Role: Build the data, decisioning and automated systems that allow Paddle to take more good risk while reducing fraud losses, unnecessary customer friction and manual work. Paddle’s Merchant of Record model makes risk a critical part of the product and its economics. Seller quality, buyer fraud, payment acceptance, refunds, disputes, reserves and card-scheme exposure cannot be optimised independently. This role will connect those signals, identify where the largest value is being lost, turn risk priorities into working controls and workflows, prove their effect in production, and establish a durable owner once a capability becomes repeatable. This is not a strategy-only role and it is not ownership of a large operational team. It is a hands-on build role at the intersection of risk, data, product, engineering and operations. What you'll do: Work hands-on with SQL (Snowflake, dbt), Python, statistics and modern AI-assisted tools to explore data, test hypotheses, prototype controls and evaluate results. Map the end-to-end seller risk system, its data, decisions, controls, owners and failure points. Establish the baseline before building: fraud losses, alert yield, time-to-detect, exposure at detection and analyst effort, with losses reconciled with Finance. Own the health of live controls: every rule and check has an owner, an expected volume, a measured yield and alerting when it goes quiet or drifts, and every change is tested and impact-assessed before release. Build and maintain a labelled library of confirmed fraud cases and a shared fraud typology: the basis for rules now and for machine-learning models with Data Science later. Build a value-ranked portfolio of risk opportunities. Translate risk problems into clear product, data and engineering work with measurable acceptance criteria. Design seller risk tiers that set payout timing, reserves and limits, giving good sellers more room and tightening controls on riskier ones. Backtest rules and risk scores on point-in-time data, and design control experiments, shadow tests and phased roll-outs that measure both loss reduction and legitimate-customer impact. Produce decision artefacts that let senior leaders make trade-offs about risk appetite, engineering investment, customer experience and commercial growth. Stay with each major capability until it works in production, then establish its long-term owner and move to the next high-value problem. Expected 6 month outcomes: At least one major seller-risk journey has materially improved on agreed loss, approval, speed or manual-effort measures. Fraud/Risk Operations spends significantly less time on repetitive screening and more time on investigation, judgement and improvement. Stable capabilities have been handed to durable owners, leaving the role free to take on the next high-value problems. We’re making conversational shopping a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey. We're designing the future of autonomous marketing , taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do. jobs.title: New Business Manager
jobs.description: Our company Surfer is an AI Visibility Platform that helps marketing teams become the definitive answer wherever their buyers search — across Google and AI search. The platform combines data, research-backed optimization, and a user-friendly workflow to grow brand visibility through content where buying decisions start to form. Surfer is used by content marketers, SEO specialists, agencies, and in-house marketing teams around the world to track, plan, write, and optimize content that gets ranked and cited by both search engines and LLMs. Surfer is part of Positive Group - a fast-growing tech group specializing in B2B SaaS products that help marketing teams grow smarter. The group brings together several brands around a common ambition: to become the European benchmark in MarTech. With around 400 employees based in France, Germany, Italy, and Poland, Positive supports customers in 80+ countries. We’re a remote-first company , but if you ever crave some in-person energy, we’ve got a cozy office in Wrocław , Poland where the magic happens (and coffee never runs out ☕). About the role We're looking for someone who's worked at a marketing/SEO agency or a martech company and knows what it takes to close - someone who picks up the phone without thinking twice, and who hasn't been trained out of that instinct by years of "process." On a day-to-day basis, you'll own the new-business side end-to-end: prospecting and building your own pipeline, working the leads that come your way, qualifying them, running discovery and demos, negotiating, and closing. You'll work closely with the Customer Success team, and get support from Marketing and RevOps. This role rewards initiative - the more you build and close, the more it shows, both in your results and in what you earn. You will be responsible for: Work both sides of the pipeline: reaching out to existing leads in our CRM (conference, meetup, webinar, and community signals plus records of past interest) while building a new pipeline from scratch through your own outbound prospecting. Prospect actively: research target accounts, identify decision-makers, and open conversations with agencies and in-house teams that haven’t reached out to us yet. Run multi-channel outreach on these leads across email, LinkedIn, and phone. Build and continuously refine ICP-aligned contact lists covering both marketing/SEO agencies and in-house SEO/marketing teams at companies. Qualify leads and run discovery calls, demos, and negotiations, owning the deal through to signed contract and payment. Requirements: Minimum 4 years of B2B sales experience as an SDR/BDR/AE at a marketing/SEO agency, a martech company (e.g. SEO, content, analytics, or marketing automation software), or at a company selling into agencies. jobs.description: About WebEngage : WebEngage is an enterprise-grade customer engagement and retention platform that helps global brands across industries such as e-commerce, fintech, travel, edtech, gaming, media, and consumer apps. and turn data into measurable revenue impact. Trusted by 800+ brands globally, we have strong presence in India, UAE, KSA, SEA, Europe and beyond. WebEngage powers intelligent, real-time engagement across the entire customer lifecycle. We are built for scale. We are built for complexity. We are built for outcomes. At our core, WebEngage is a full-stack retention operating system that combines: A powerful Customer Data Platform (CDP) Real-time behavioral segmentation and intelligence Omnichannel journey orchestration AI-driven personalization and recommendations Deep analytics, experimentation, and revenue attribution WebEngage BLACK: our AI-native layer that brings Agentic capabilities to engagement. Learn more about us at www.webengage.com About The Role: WebEngage ’s Data Engineering team is the backbone of our analytics, personalisation, and machine-learning capabilities. As a Data Engineer, you will own the end-to-end lifecycle of data — from ingesting raw event streams and third-party feeds to building well-modelled, highly reliable datasets that power dashboards, predictive models, and customer journey orchestration. This is a high-impact, hands-on role where you will work at the intersection of product, analytics, and backend engineering. You will be expected to think beyond just moving data — designing for data quality, pipeline observability, cost efficiency, and long-term maintainability from day one. Responsibilities: Pipeline Development & Reliability Design, build, and maintain production-grade ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest data from APIs, databases, event streams (Kafka/Pub-Sub), and flat files into the central data warehouse. Implement idempotent, incremental load patterns with built-in retry logic, dead-letter queues, and SLA-based alerting to ensure zero-data-loss pipelines. Own pipeline observability — set up data freshness checks, row-count validations, schema drift detection, and anomaly alerts using tools like Great Expectations or dbt tests. Data Modelling & Warehouse Design Translate business requirements into clean dimensional models (star/snowflake schemas) and maintain a well-documented data catalogue. Design slowly changing dimensions (SCD Type 1/2), bridge tables, and fact tables optimised for analytical query patterns. Enforce partitioning, clustering, and materialised view strategies to keep warehouse costs under control while maintaining sub-second query performance. Code Quality & Engineering Best Practices Write clean, modular, well-tested Python and SQL code. Follow DRY principles, use version control (Git), and participate in peer code reviews. Build reusable transformation frameworks using dbt or equivalent tooling, with proper documentation and testing at every layer (staging → intermediate → mart). Containerise data services with Docker and automate deployments via CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions / GitLab CI). BI, Visualization & Analytics Build interactive dashboards and analytical tools using Streamlit, enabling stakeholders to explore metrics, run ad-hoc analyses, and make data-driven decisions without engineering dependency. Design and maintain BI layers — semantic models, KPI definitions, and pre-aggregated mart tables that serve as the single source of truth for reporting across teams. Translate raw data into compelling visual narratives using libraries like Plotly, Matplotlib, or Altair; present findings to both technical and non-technical audiences. Collaboration & Communication Partner with product managers, analysts, and data scientists to understand data needs and proactively identify gaps in current data coverage. Document data lineage, transformation logic, SLAs, and known limitations in a shared knowledge base to enable self-service analytics.

Could you lead ops coordinators, project managers and service teams while carrying real projects alongside them? On a typical day you might run the planning call for a cross-team project you are leading, review a dashboard showing which requests are running late, sit with a pod lead to rebuild an estimate that looks twice as long as the last similar job, and agree with the Internal Product team which manual handoff to automate next. About Contour We operate across three brands. The India team, part of the Global Enablement and Support pillar, is the global capability centre (GCC) Contour is building. It runs delivery, automation, people and operations for the whole organisation, working closely with teams in Australia. The kind of people who thrive here Contour started in 2020 as one classroom in a university library. In 2022 three full-time team members ran the business on. Today we are about 600 people across Australia and India, and much of what we run was built by someone who noticed it was missing. The work matters. More than 10,000 students rely on what we build, from the booklets they study from to the systems their families pay through. People who do well here care about that. They own their work end to end, start things without being asked and finish what they commit to. They tell the truth early, write decisions down and give direct feedback. The pace is fast: small problems are fixed the same week, bigger ones within the six-week cycle. Growth follows what you deliver: scope, title and pay move with the bar you raise. About this role You lead Operations in Contour's India team: several teams brought together under one player-coach. Your team includes Contour’s operations coordinators, who keep academics, campus, finance and the founder’s office running day to day, and its project coordinators and managers, who run cross-team work across the business. It also covers organisation services such as print operations, procurement and workspace systems. Each service has two sides. In Australia, a functional owner, such as Finance or Academics, sets its standards and priorities. In India, you run the work: coordinators and project managers report to you directly, and any service big enough for its own pod lead reports through them. Everything else is yours: how work comes in, how it is planned, checked and automated, and how the people doing it grow. Two things separate a strong hire here from a competent one. First, you learn each service's workflow well enough to coach its lead, inspect what it produces and challenge its estimates, and you know where your knowledge stops: on professional questions, you rely on the specialists. Second, you make different services run as one, with a shared way of taking requests, planning capacity and checking work, so the rest of Contour deals with one group rather than a row of separate desks. This is a player-coach seat, and we mean it. Expect a real share of most weeks to go on doing the work yourself: running a cross-team project end to end, taking the coordination nobody else can untangle, checking a sample of finished work, mapping a process that keeps stalling or rebuilding an estimate from the ground up. The rest goes on making your coordinators, project managers and pod leads better at the same work. You won't be the specialist in every service, but you can work inside each one's workflow, and your team sees you do it. Contour is scaling and hires for the long term: the scope of this seat grows with the platform, and what you deliver decides how fast. The intake, planning, quality and automation routines you set now are what every later service joins.
